mt: 'TAPER MAGAZINE' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE MAGAZINE IN ITS OWN WORDS; ITS SIZE LIMIT AND AN MIT LAB FROM CARDS; ITS SIXTEENTH ISSUE DATED BY A CARD A SEASON BEFORE THE INDEX DATES IT; NO PIECE AND NO AUTHOR
d: THE MAGAZINE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'Taper is an online literary magazine for small computational pieces:' with a link to the site; what it is: format ('A browser-based, biannual online literary journal and digital zine'), constraint ('strictly under 2 kilobytes (2048 bytes) in size (HTML5/code-based)'), publisher ('Published by Bad Quarto, historically coordinated with MIT's The Trope Tank'), history ('Launched in Spring 2018 with Issue #1 (a minimal labyrinth), and has grown past 16 issues (such as Taper #16: For Good Measure) managed by a volunteer editorial collective'); an offer on past themes or submitting. Six cards: taper.badquar.to (twice), Helen Shewolfe Tseng, Instagram, anjchang.com, Facebook.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the magazine, the Overview gives its own description, then its format, size limit, publisher and history, from its index page, a contributor's page and its social accounts.
findings: THE MAGAZINE IN ITS OWN WORDS. The first line is the index page's self-description to the comma: 'an online literary magazine for small computational pieces, published by Bad Quarto'. Bad Quarto as publisher and the first issue agree with the page: 'Taper #1 : a minimal labyrinth, Spring 2018.'

THE LIMIT AND THE LAB FROM CARDS. 'strictly under 2 kilobytes (2048 bytes)' follows the Instagram card ('Taper is a browser-based literary magazine for computational poems under 2KB (2048 bytes)') and Tseng's ('tiny computational poems (under 2 kilobytes)'); 'historically coordinated with MIT's The Trope Tank' follows the anjchang card ('published by Bad Quarto in coordination with MIT's T...'). The saved index page states neither. 'managed by a volunteer editorial collective' is on no saved page and no card.

THE ISSUES AND THEIR DATES. 'has grown past 16 issues (such as Taper #16: For Good Measure)'. The index lists sixteen, the last 'Taper #16 : for good measure, Spring 2026.', with 'The call for work for issue #17 is also available!'; the Instagram card carries that call ('Submit your 2Kb HTML5 digital poems to Taper 17: Prime'). The Facebook card dates the sixteenth issue a season earlier: 'Aug 6, 2025 — Taper #16: For Good Measure is out now! ... by 23 authors'; the index gives 'Taper #15 : crossroads, Fall 2025.' The census row takes the index's dates. Its 'two issues a year' and the composition's 'biannual' both pass over the index's gap between 'Taper #3 : triptychs and triads, Spring 2019.' and 'Taper #4 : a new trope, Spring 2020.'

NO PIECE AND NO AUTHOR. The census row records the name of a piece's maker as 'not recorded on the saved index page, which lists issues only'. The composition names no piece and no author; the cards count and name contributors ('by 23 authors'; Tseng, 'I have been a contributor since Spring 2022'). Its account of the work is of form, 'tiny computational poems and web art', read in a browser; the census row's reading holds that 'Computational form alone does not establish composition addressed to machine reception', and the composition names no machine addressee either.
analysis: The magazine composed in its own words, with a size limit, a lab and a collective drawn from cards and from no saved page, and a sixteenth issue that a card dates to August 2025 and the index to Spring 2026. No piece or author is named.
per_note: Bad Quarto and MIT's Trope Tank named; no editor or author; the magazine's index carded twice.
